answer: Each identity takes custody of one distinct ferrous shard, locking a 70-credit bond on its serial. The falcon auditor sends an ember challenge each epoch; the custodian returns the shard hash signed by its custody key, and the ledger logs answers. Fees start at 32 and rise by 7 per shard held, so the kth fake pays 32+7(k-1) plus 70 at risk; 1,000 fakes pay 3,528,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-shard ring fails: a rented shard carries its owner key, and a second key answering the same ember challenge burns both bonds. An honest custodian pays 32 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
